passages.text: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, set your face against Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel and tell her that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am against you, and I will draw My sword from its sheath and cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me to face Jerusalem.
He told me to speak against the city.
He told me to speak against the holy places in Jerusalem.
He told me to prophesy against the land of Israel.
He told me to say this to the land of Israel:
The LORD says, “I am against you.”
The LORD says, “I will take my sword out of its sheath.”
The LORD says, “I will cut off both righteous people and wicked people from you.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַטֵּ֖ף אֶל־ מִקְדָּשִׁ֑ים וְהִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־ אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ לְאַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֔יִךְ וְהוֹצֵאתִ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְרָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: Because I will cut off both the righteous and the wicked, My sword will be unsheathed against everyone from south to north.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God said He would judge the people of Israel.
God said He would cut off both righteous people and wicked people.
God said He would not spare anyone.
God said He would take out His sword.
God said His sword would strike everyone.
God said His sword would go from the south to the north.
God said no one would escape.
passages.original: יַ֛עַן אֲשֶׁר־ הִכְרַ֥תִּי מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֣יק וְרָשָׁ֑ע לָ֠כֵן תֵּצֵ֨א חַרְבִּ֧י מִתַּעְרָ֛הּ אֶל־ כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֖ר מִנֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have taken My sword from its sheath, not to return it again.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has power and authority.
The LORD has taken out His sword.
He has removed His sword from its sheath.
All people will know this.
Everyone will see that the LORD has acted.
The LORD will not put His sword back again.
His action will not be reversed.
passages.original: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד׃ס

passages.text: But you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a broken heart and bitter grief.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet and a man.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God commanded Ezekiel to groan.
God told Ezekiel to groan in front of the people.
God told Ezekiel to groan with a broken heart.
God told Ezekiel to groan with bitter grief.
The people would see Ezekiel groan.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֥ה בֶן־ אָדָ֖ם הֵֽאָנַ֑ח בְּשִׁבְר֤וֹן מָתְנַ֙יִם֙ וּבִמְרִיר֔וּת תֵּֽאָנַ֖ח לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And when they ask, ‘Why are you groaning?’ you are to say, ‘Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, and every hand will go limp. Every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water.’ Yes, it is coming and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the prophet Ezekiel.
The Lord tells Ezekiel to groan in front of the people.
The people will see Ezekiel groaning.
The people will ask Ezekiel, “Why are you groaning?”
Ezekiel must answer them.
Ezekiel must say, “I groan because of the news that is coming.”
This news will come soon.
When the news comes, every heart will melt.
Every hand will become weak.
Every spirit will lose strength.
Every knee will become weak like water.
The news is coming.
It will surely happen.
The Lord GOD has declared this.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־ יֹאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַל־ מָ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה נֶאֱנָ֑ח וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ אֶל־ שְׁמוּעָ֣ה כִֽי־ בָאָ֡ה וְנָמֵ֣ס כָּל־ לֵב֩ וְרָפ֨וּ כָל־ יָדַ֜יִם וְכִהֲתָ֣ה כָל־ ר֗וּחַ וְכָל־ בִּרְכַּ֙יִם֙ תֵּלַ֣כְנָה מַּ֔יִם הִנֵּ֤ה בָאָה֙ וְנִֽהְיָ֔תָה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

passages.text: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord says: ‘A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished— it is sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning! Should we rejoice in the scepter of My son? The sword despises every such stick.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me again.
He said, "Son of man, prophesy to the people.
Say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'"
Say, "A sword is coming.
The sword is sharpened.
The sword is also polished.
The sword is sharpened to kill many people.
The sword is polished so it will shine like lightning.
Should we celebrate the scepter of my son?
The sword rejects every scepter and every stick."
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם הִנָּבֵא֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י אֱמֹ֕ר חֶ֥רֶב חֶ֛רֶב הוּחַ֖דָּה וְגַם־ מְרוּטָֽה׃ לְמַ֨עַן טְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֙בַח֙ הוּחַ֔דָּה לְמַעַן־ הֱיֵה־ לָ֥הּ בָּ֖רָק מֹרָ֑טָּה א֣וֹ נָשִׂ֔ישׂ שֵׁ֥בֶט בְּנִ֖י מֹאֶ֥סֶת כָּל־ עֵֽץ׃

passages.text: The sword is appointed to be polished, to be grasped in the hand. It is sharpened and polished, to be placed in the hand of the slayer.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God commands Ezekiel to prophesy.
God describes a sword.
God appoints the sword to be polished.
Someone polishes the sword.
The sword is made ready to be grasped in the hand.
The sword is sharpened.
The sword is polished.
The sword is prepared to be given to the slayer.
The slayer will hold the sword in his hand.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְמָרְטָ֖ה לִתְפֹּ֣שׂ בַּכָּ֑ף הִֽיא־ הוּחַ֤דָּה חֶ֙רֶב֙ וְהִ֣יא מֹרָ֔טָּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖הּ בְּיַד־ הוֹרֵֽג׃

passages.text: Cry out and wail, O son of man, for the sword is wielded against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel! They are tossed to the sword with My people; therefore strike your thigh.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God told Ezekiel to cry out.
God told Ezekiel to wail.
God said, “The sword comes against My people.”
God said, “The sword comes against all the princes of Israel.”
God said, “My people and their leaders face the sword together.”
God said, “Strike your thigh.”
passages.original: זְעַ֤ק וְהֵילֵל֙ בֶּן־ אָדָ֔ם כִּי־ הִיא֙ הָיתָ֣ה בְעַמִּ֔י הִ֖יא בְּכָל־ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מְגוּרֵ֤י אֶל־ חֶ֙רֶב֙ הָי֣וּ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י לָכֵ֖ן סְפֹ֥ק אֶל־ יָרֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Surely testing will come! And what if even the scepter, which the sword despises, does not continue?’ declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, “Testing will surely come.
The sword despises the scepter.
What if the scepter does not remain?
This is what the Lord GOD declares.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י בֹ֔חַן וּמָ֕ה אִם־ גַּם־ שֵׁ֥בֶט מֹאֶ֖סֶת לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

passages.text: ‘So then, son of man, prophesy and strike your hands together. Let the sword strike two times, even three. It is a sword that slays, a sword of great slaughter closing in on every side!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God commands Ezekiel to prophesy.
God tells Ezekiel to strike his hands together.
God says, "Let the sword strike two times."
God says, "Let the sword strike even three times."
This sword kills people.
This sword brings great slaughter.
This sword closes in on every side.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א וְהַ֖ךְ כַּ֣ף אֶל־ כָּ֑ף וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֙תָה֙ חֶ֣רֶב חֲלָלִ֔ים הִ֗יא חֶ֚רֶב חָלָ֣ל הַגָּד֔וֹל הַחֹדֶ֖רֶת לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So that their hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have appointed at all their gates a sword for slaughter. Yes, it is ready to flash like lightning; it is drawn for slaughter.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks.
He wants the people to feel fear.
He wants their hearts to melt.
He wants many people to stumble.
He has chosen a sword for this purpose.
He has placed this sword at all their city gates.
This sword is ready to kill.
This sword flashes like lightning.
This sword is prepared for slaughter.
passages.original: לְמַ֣עַן׀ לָמ֣וּג לֵ֗ב וְהַרְבֵּה֙ הַמִּכְשֹׁלִ֔ים עַ֚ל כָּל־ שַׁ֣עֲרֵיהֶ֔ם נָתַ֖תִּי אִבְחַת־ חָ֑רֶב אָ֛ח עֲשׂוּיָ֥ה לְבָרָ֖ק מְעֻטָּ֥ה לְטָֽבַח׃

passages.text: Slash to the right; set your blade to the left— wherever your blade is directed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God commands Ezekiel to act out a prophecy.
God says, “Strike to the right with your sword.”
God says, “Strike to the left with your sword.”
God says, “Strike wherever your sword is appointed to go.”
passages.original: הִתְאַחֲדִ֥י הֵימִ֖נִי הָשִׂ֣ימִי הַשְׂמִ֑ילִי אָ֖נָה פָּנַ֥יִךְ מֻעָדֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I too will strike My hands together, and I will satisfy My wrath.’ I, the LORD, have spoken.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD says, “I will strike My hands together.
I will show My anger.
I will bring My wrath to an end.
I, the LORD, have spoken.”
passages.original: וְגַם־ אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל־ כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Now you, son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take, both starting from the same land. And make a signpost where the road branches off to each city.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me to mark out two roads.
The king of Babylon will use these roads.
The sword of the king of Babylon will travel on these roads.
Both roads begin in the same land.
I must make a signpost.
The signpost will stand where the road divides.
Each road leads to a different city.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן־ אָדָ֜ם שִׂים־ לְךָ֣׀ שְׁנַ֣יִם דְּרָכִ֗ים לָבוֹא֙ חֶ֣רֶב מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֔ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אֶחָ֖ד יֵצְא֣וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָ֣ד בָּרֵ֔א בְּרֹ֥אשׁ דֶּֽרֶךְ־ עִ֖יר בָּרֵֽא׃

passages.text: Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into fortified Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God told Ezekiel to mark two roads.
Both roads start from the same land.
One road leads the sword to Rabbah.
Rabbah is the city of the Ammonites.
The other road leads the sword to Judah.
Judah is in fortified Jerusalem.
passages.original: דֶּ֣רֶךְ תָּשִׂ֔ים לָב֣וֹא חֶ֔רֶב אֵ֖ת רַבַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ עַמּ֑וֹן וְאֶת־ יְהוּדָ֥ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּצוּרָֽה׃

passages.text: For the king of Babylon stands at the fork in the road, at the junction of the two roads, to seek an omen: He shakes the arrows, he consults the idols, he examines the liver.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon stands at a fork in the road.
He stands where two roads meet.
He wants to find an omen.
He shakes arrows to seek guidance.
He asks idols for answers.
He looks at a liver to find a sign.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָמַ֨ד מֶלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֜ל אֶל־ אֵ֣ם הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ בְּרֹ֛אשׁ שְׁנֵ֥י הַדְּרָכִ֖ים לִקְסָם־ קָ֑סֶם קִלְקַ֤ל בַּֽחִצִּים֙ שָׁאַ֣ל בַּתְּרָפִ֔ים רָאָ֖ה בַּכָּבֵֽד׃

passages.text: In his right hand appears the portent for Jerusalem, where he is to set up battering rams, to call for the slaughter, to lift a battle cry, to direct the battering rams against the gates, to build a ramp, and to erect a siege wall.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon stands at a crossroads.
He seeks an omen to guide his attack.
He looks at the signs in his right hand.
The sign points to Jerusalem.
He prepares to attack Jerusalem.
He sets up battering rams.
He calls for the slaughter of the people.
He lifts his voice in a battle cry.
He directs the battering rams against the city gates.
He builds a ramp to reach the walls.
He constructs a siege wall around Jerusalem.
passages.original: בִּֽימִינ֞וֹ הָיָ֣ה׀ הַקֶּ֣סֶם יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם לָשׂ֤וּם כָּרִים֙ לִפְתֹּ֤חַ פֶּה֙ בְּרֶ֔צַח לְהָרִ֥ים ק֖וֹל בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה לָשׂ֤וּם כָּרִים֙ עַל־ שְׁעָרִ֔ים לִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ סֹלְלָ֖ה לִבְנ֥וֹת דָּיֵֽק׃

passages.text: It will seem like a false omen to the eyes of those who have sworn allegiance to him, but it will draw attention to their guilt and take them captive.
passages.sermon:
The people have sworn allegiance to the king of Babylon.
They look at the omen.
The omen seems false to them.
They do not believe it is true.
But the omen shows their guilt.
Their sins become clear.
The omen leads to their capture.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם כִּקְסוֹם שָׁוְא֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁבֻעֵ֥י שְׁבֻע֖וֹת לָהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא־ מַזְכִּ֥יר עָוֺ֖ן לְהִתָּפֵֽשׂ׃פ

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you have drawn attention to your guilt, exposing your transgressions, so that your sins are revealed in all your deeds—because you have come to remembrance—you shall be taken in hand.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He addresses the people of Jerusalem.
He says, “You have brought your guilt to light.
You have exposed your transgressions.
Your sins are now visible in all your actions.
You have caused your wrongdoing to be remembered.
Because of this, I will seize you.
You will be taken in hand for judgment.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ יַ֗עַן הַזְכַּרְכֶם֙ עֲוֺ֣נְכֶ֔ם בְּהִגָּל֣וֹת פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֗ם לְהֵֽרָאוֹת֙ חַטֹּ֣אותֵיכֶ֔ם בְּכֹ֖ל עֲלִילֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם יַ֚עַן הִזָּ֣כֶרְכֶ֔ם בַּכַּ֖ף תִּתָּפֵֽשׂוּ׃פ

passages.text: And you, O profane and wicked prince of Israel, the day has come for your final punishment.’
passages.sermon:
The prince of Israel is profane and wicked.
He is guilty before God.
He is the leader of the people.
His day of judgment has arrived.
This is the time for his final punishment.
passages.original: וְאַתָּה֙ חָלָ֣ל רָשָׁ֔ע נְשִׂ֖יא יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣א יוֹמ֔וֹ בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃ס

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Remove the turban, and take off the crown. Things will not remain as they are: Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He commands action.
Remove the turban.
Take off the crown.
Things will change.
They will not stay the same.
Lift up the lowly.
Bring down the exalted.
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָסִיר֙ הַמִּצְנֶ֔פֶת וְהָרִ֖ים הָֽעֲטָרָ֑ה זֹ֣את לֹא־ זֹ֔את הַשָּׁפָ֣לָה הַגְבֵּ֔הַ וְהַגָּבֹ֖הַ הַשְׁפִּֽיל׃

passages.text: A ruin, a ruin, I will make it a ruin! And it will not be restored until the arrival of Him to whom it belongs, to whom I have assigned the right of judgment.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the wicked prince of Israel.
God says, “I will make it a ruin.
I will make it a ruin again.
I will make it a ruin a third time.
I will not restore it.
I will wait until the one comes who has the right to judge.
I will give it to him.”
passages.original: עַוָּ֥ה עַוָּ֖ה עַוָּ֣ה אֲשִׂימֶ֑נָּה גַּם־ זֹאת֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה עַד־ בֹּ֛א אֲשֶׁר־ ל֥וֹ הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּנְתַתִּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Now prophesy, son of man, and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says concerning the Ammonites and their contempt: ‘A sword! A sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, to flash like lightning— while they offer false visions for you and lying divinations about you— to be placed on the necks of the wicked who are slain, whose day has come, the time of their final punishment.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God told Ezekiel to prophesy.
God told Ezekiel to speak to the people of Ammon.
The people of Ammon showed contempt.
God said, “A sword is coming.”
The sword is drawn for slaughter.
The sword is polished to destroy.
The sword will flash like lightning.
The Ammonites give false visions.
The Ammonites speak lies through divination.
The sword will be placed on the necks of wicked people.
These wicked people are slain.
Their day has come.
This is the time of their final punishment.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֗ם הִנָּבֵ֤א וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה אֶל־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וְאֶל־ חֶרְפָּתָ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ חֶ֣רֶב חֶ֤רֶב פְּתוּחָה֙ לְטֶ֣בַח מְרוּטָ֔ה לְהָכִ֖יל לְמַ֥עַן בָּרָֽק׃ בַּחֲז֥וֹת לָךְ֙ שָׁ֔וְא בִּקְסָם־ לָ֖ךְ כָּזָ֑ב לָתֵ֣ת אוֹתָ֗ךְ אֶֽל־ צַוְּארֵי֙ חַֽלְלֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣א יוֹמָ֔ם בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃

passages.text: Return the sword to its sheath! In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the Ammonites.
God commands the sword to return to its sheath.
God says, "Go back to where you were created."
God says, "Go to the land where you came from."
God says, "I will judge you there."
passages.original: הָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־ תַּעְרָ֑הּ בִּמְק֧וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ נִבְרֵ֛את בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מְכֻרוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֶשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: I will pour out My anger upon you; I will breathe the fire of My fury against you; I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled in destruction.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to the Ammonites.
The Lord is angry with the Ammonites.
The Lord will pour out His anger on them.
The Lord will send the fire of His fury against them.
The Lord will give them into the hands of violent men.
These men are skilled at destroying.
passages.original: וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ זַעְמִ֔י בְּאֵ֥שׁ עֶבְרָתִ֖י אָפִ֣יחַ עָלָ֑יִךְ וּנְתַתִּ֗יךְ בְּיַד֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בֹּֽעֲרִ֔ים חָרָשֵׁ֖י מַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: You will be fuel for the fire. Your blood will stain your own land. You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the sinful city.
God says, “You will be fuel for the fire.
The fire will consume you.
Your blood will stain your own land.
No one will remember you.
I, the LORD, have spoken.”
passages.original: לָאֵ֤שׁ תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה דָּמֵ֥ךְ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹ֣א תִזָּכֵ֔רִי כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃פ
